Multi-group clustering of age specific trends

Source: R/cluster.R
jp_cluster.Rd

Clusters contiguous age groups whose trends are as parallel as possible and fits a joinpoint model to the age adjusted rates of each cluster: pre-analysis count compression, parallel joinpoint fits for every block of contiguous age groups, the partition into m clusters with minimum total residual sum of squares, selection of m by BIC, and optional clustering MADWD.

Usage

jp_cluster(
  data,
  x,
  count,
  population,
  age,
  standard,
  by = NULL,
  delay = NULL,
  min_count = 0,
  compression = c("forward", "backward"),
  method = c("wbic", "bic", "bic3", "permutation"),
  max_clusters = NULL,
  madwd = NULL,
  kmin = 0,
  kmax = NULL,
  final_method = "wbic",
  rate_per = 1e+05,
  control = jp_control(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per age group and time point (and cohort).

x

Column of the independent variable (time).

count, population

Columns of counts and populations.

age

Column of age groups. For clustering their order matters: the levels of a factor, numeric order, or the leading number of each label (for example "0-4", "5-9", "85+").

standard

Either a column of data holding the standard population of each row, or a numeric vector named by age group (for example from std_populations).

by

Optional character vector of by-variables.

delay

Optional column of delay factors (1 to 20).

min_count

Age groups are combined until counts exceed this value at every time point.

compression

"forward" or "backward" count compression.

method

Method for the number of joinpoints within clustering: "wbic", "bic", "bic3" or "permutation".

max_clusters

Maximum number of clusters (default: number of compressed age groups).

madwd

Clustering minimum APC difference worth detecting, in percentage points (NULL to disable).

kmin, kmax

Minimum and maximum number of joinpoints.

final_method

Model selection method for the final fits of the cluster age adjusted rates (see joinpoint()).

rate_per

Rate multiplier.

control

Settings from jp_control(), used for the clustering fits and the final fits.

...

Further arguments to joinpoint() for the final cluster fits (for example ci_method).

Value

An object of class jp_cluster with the compressed age groups, the cluster selection table, the final clusters, the MADWD steps, the cluster rates and fit, the joinpoint() fit of the cluster age adjusted rates.

Examples

set.seed(1)
ages <- c("40-49", "50-59", "60-69", "70-79")
d <- expand.grid(year = 2000:2019, age = ages, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
d$pop <- 1e5
slope <- ifelse(d$age %in% ages[1:2], 0.03, -0.02)
d$count <- rpois(nrow(d), 200 * exp(slope * (d$year - 2000)))
cl <- jp_cluster(d, year, count, pop, age, standard = setNames(rep(1, 4), ages),
                 kmax = 1, ci_method = "parametric")
cl$clusters
#>          cluster age_group
#> 1 40-49 to 50-59     40-49
#> 2 40-49 to 50-59     50-59
#> 3 60-69 to 70-79     60-69
#> 4 60-69 to 70-79     70-79
